A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same ASCOOD study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original ASCOOD and i-ODIN experiments, classification accuracies, and ablations across spurious, fine-grained, and conventional OOD settings.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices C–G, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and feature visualizations.

M1.justification: Outlier synthesis, standardized features, training losses, and inference procedures are unchanged. The revised description of i-ODIN's variable selection mask matches the top-k masking procedure already specified in v3 Appendix B.

E1.justification: The same datasets and spurious, fine-grained, conventional, and near-OOD scenarios remain represented. ImageNet-200/1k i-ODIN evaluations also remain in Appendix G.1; reorganizing the main tables does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: The reported ASCOOD comparisons lose ODIN/i-ODIN entries for Waterbirds and CelebA spurious OOD, without equivalent numerical comparisons elsewhere in v4. Table 3 also drops i-ODIN from ImageNet-100. OE and MixOE move into the consolidated Table 1 but were already evaluated in v3.

E3.justification: Retained experiments use the same splits, metrics, architectures, training budgets, and postprocessor tuning. Training settings move from Appendix D into Section 4; the PDFs do not establish changed experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The synthesis, normalization, loss, and hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged, as do the UMAP and confidence-distribution analyses. The revised main-text i-ODIN table redisplays existing comparisons rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: v4 Table 1 first supplies ± uncertainty values for the existing OE/MixOE comparisons on Aircraft, Car, Waterbirds, and CelebA. v3 Table 5 reported only point estimates for these comparisons. No additional run counts, seeds, or statistical procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: Some results disappear, including i-ODIN's ImageNet-100 average of 41.23/88.81. The consolidated Waterbirds ASCOOD result uses 11.37/97.48 instead of v3 Table 5's conflicting 12.23/97.40, aligning with v3 Table 1 rather than demonstrating a new gain. The new 33% i-ODIN statement incorrectly names CIFAR-100 as ID; Table 4 supports CIFAR-10-to-TIN.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, two propositions and their proofs, training objective, and Appendix B perturbation equations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit first-demonstration claim about gradient addition versus subtraction and promotes z-score superiority over L2 normalization to a contribution. These sharpen the novelty claims around existing evidence; the central unified OOD-detection contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an explanation that external OE/MixOE outliers may lack or more strongly degrade spurious environmental features. It also newly qualifies i-ODIN's applicability by stating that its improvement is absent in the two-class Waterbirds/CelebA cases.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies 224×224 inputs for ImageNet-100. Conversely, v4 removes the explicit code-availability statement and repository link. Most training details are relocated unchanged, so their appearance in Section 4 is not new disclosure.

R1.justification: v4 adds 17 cited works and substantially expands positioning against image-space outlier synthesis, including Kirby, BackMix, OEST, and foundation-model approaches. It acknowledges shared invariant-feature removal with close predecessors and distinguishes ASCOOD through gradient addition and challenging outlier construction.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, motivation, and contribution bullets are substantially revised. Training details move into the main experiments section, while the results narrative is reordered to lead with fine-grained detection and integrate previously separate OE comparisons.

P2.justification: The main experimental presentation is substantially rebuilt: Table 1 consolidates selected results from several former tables and appendix comparisons, while Table 4 replaces the aggregate i-ODIN overview with selected challenging cases. Metric columns, dataset ordering, and table/figure placement change; the underlying illustrations and appendix plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves research positioning and uncertainty reporting for existing OE/MixOE comparisons. However, it removes code-access information and some comparator results, and introduces the incorrect CIFAR-100-to-TIN attribution in its i-ODIN summary. These concrete gains and losses leave the net effect on paper quality unclear, with the central methods, experiments, and proofs otherwise retained.
